validated_results.title: Dietary B group vitamin intake and the bladder cancer risk: a pooled analysis of prospective cohort studies.
validated_results.reason: Prospective pooled cohort analysis evaluating dietary vitamin B1 intake and incident bladder cancer risk with quantitative effect estimates.

extraction.population: General adult population from four prospective cohort studies in the BLEND consortium

cases.excerpt: In total, 2915 BC cases and 530,012 non-cases were included in the analyses.

comparison.excerpt: B group vitamin intake was classified in tertiles (low/moderate/high intake) based on the distribution of all included study participants per study separately

effect_size.excerpt: Overall, a decreased MIBC risk was observed for high intake of the vitamins B1, B2, B3, B6, B9 the vitamins related to energy metabolism, oxidative stress reduction and DNA stability (HR B1 : 0.86, 95% CI: 0.77–0.97, HR B2 : 0.88, 95% CI: 0.78–0.98, HR B3 : 0.80, 95% CI: 0.72–0.90, HR B6 : 0.88, 95% CI: 0.79–0.99, HR B9 : 0.86, 95% CI: 0.77–0.96, HR energy metabolism : 0.84, 95% CI: 0.75–0.95, HR oxidative stress : 0.88, 95% CI: 0.79–0.98, HR DNA stability : 0.85, 95% CI: 0.75–0.95) (Table 4 ).
